# Introduction

The purpose of this page is to demonstrate various code chunks and features of the Quarto Web Tufte setup, and save them for further use later.

This is an attempt to understand how to best render attractive text in a web format according to the tufte style. It turns out that one of the easiest ways to do this (in a widely supported format) is via quarto, which has an [excellent demonstration](https://quarto-dev.github.io/quarto-gallery/page-layout/tufte.html) of how this works.

# General Inventory

- Looks like footnotes are handled natively.[^1]

[^1]: That is, you can just write them in markdown as normal, and given the `yaml` config in the header, they will be placed in the margin.




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Code blocks also work as you would expect them to,
# and render in the page directly on knitting.

1 + 1
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 2
```


:::
:::




- You can also specify a bibtext file in the `yaml` header, and, when in `Visual` mode within the RStudio IDE, it will read the file and auto-complete citations, letting you embed them (with marginal full cites) in text like this: [@wilson2023].

- You can also specify arbitrary marginal content (the rendered version is seen to the right) by enclosing it in `column-margin` blocks as below:

::: column-margin
![The cover of a great, recent album, *Bushido*, from the [Melo Music Group](https://www.mellomusicgroup.com)](images/Bushido_Cover.jpg)

Notably, formatting and links render correctly within links.
:::

```         
    ::: column-margin
    [arbitrary content]
    :::
```

- It is relatively straightforward to render a plot in the "main column", simply by executing a code block.




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = hp)) + geom_point()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Demo_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::




- Full-width content is easy, again by enclosing it in a code block like this:[^2]

[^2]: To get the image to properly render across the whole page, you need to add `.column-page-right`!

```         
    ::: {.fullwidth .column-page-right}
    Any _full width_ content here.
    :::
```

::: {.fullwidth .column-page-right}
![A banner](images/mid_goh.jpg)
:::
